d: Hays are working with a boutique family-focused Company Service Provider, part of a wider global group, as they setting up a new office in DIFC and looking to appoint a Compliance Officer & MLRO Officer. This is a rare opportunity to build the compliance function from the ground up, working alongside a leading law firm to shape the framework.

The selected professional be responsible for will implementing and maintaining the compliance framework and AML/CFT/CPF and sanctions program, acting as designated MLRO and principal point of contact for all matters. They will oversee client onboarding, KYC/CDD/EDD and risk assessments, and support the DFSA application and ongoing regulatory engagement. The role reports to the Senior Executive Officer, with independent access to the Board on MLRO matters.
q: Minimum 5 years’ compliance, AML or regulatory experience in the UAE with DIFC/DFSA exposure (ADGM experience also considered)
Strong knowledge of the DFSA AML Rulebook and UAE Federal AML/CFT requirements
Background in a corporate service provider or regulated financial services environment (in-house or consultancy)
CAMS, ICA, CISI or equivalent preferred
Hands-on, proactive and confident, with sound judgement and the ability to make decisions in a lean, growing team
The client is offering a competitive package and a unique opportunity to join a newly established entity in the DIFC under the group.
To apply or for a confidential discussion, please follow the link and apply directly.

d: Goodman Masson is partnering with a new financial markets venture under formation in Oman. Backed by prominent institutional investors, the business is building its operations from the ground up and is now hiring during the build phase.

This is an opportunity to join at an early stage and help ensure that products, services and operating frameworks are aligned with applicable regulations, the company’s rule book and participant agreements.

The Product Regulatory Analyst will work closely with Product Development to review new and existing product features, identify regulatory gaps and recommend practical solutions before products or changes are launched.

The role will also support engagement with the regulator, including contributing to the development of regulations where the company’s services are not yet covered by an established framework. You will work collaboratively with product, legal, compliance, risk and operations teams to support strong regulatory governance as the business develops.
q: A bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Business, Economics or a related discipline.
Relevant experience in regulatory compliance, legal or product-related roles, ideally within financial services or payments.
A sound understanding of financial services regulation, rule books, participant agreements and product lifecycle processes.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret regulatory requirements and identify gaps or potential risks.
Excellent drafting, documentation and communication skills, with close attention to detail.
The ability to collaborate effectively with product teams and other stakeholders.
Fluency in written and spoken English.
Experience supporting regulatory engagement or contributing to regulatory or policy drafting.
A recognised qualification in compliance, regulation or risk management.
Experience working in a developing or evolving regulatory environment.
Based in Muscat, Oman. Permanent for Omani nationals; two-year fixed-term contract for expatriate hires. Omani nationals are strongly encouraged to apply.
If you have a sound understanding of financial services regulation, this is an opportunity to help build the operational foundations of a new financial markets venture. Please apply now!
r: Review product features against applicable regulations, the company’s rule book and participant agreements.
Identify, document and assess compliance gaps, recommending practical remediation actions to product teams and management.
Support Product Development in working with the regulator to help draft regulations where existing frameworks do not yet cover the company’s services.
Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on current and planned products.
Maintain clear records of regulatory reviews, findings, recommendations and agreed actions to support audit and governance requirements.
Work with internal stakeholders to resolve regulatory matters and escalate material compliance gaps or risks appropriately.
Contribute to the development of robust regulatory processes and documentation as the venture grows.

d: Established in 1964 as the country’s first Qatari-owned commercial bank, QNB Group has steadily grown to become the largest bank in the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region.

QNB Group’s presence through its subsidiaries and associate companies extends to more than 31 countries across three continents providing a comprehensive range of advanced products and services. The total number of employees is more than 28,000 serving up to 20 million customers operating through 1,000 locations, with an ATM network of 4,300 machines.

QNB has maintained its position as one of the highest rated regional banks from leading credit rating agencies including Standard & Poor’s (A), Moody’s (Aa3) and Fitch (A+). The Bank has also been the recipient of many awards from leading international specialised financial publications.

Based on the Group’s consistent strong financial performance and its expanding international presence, QNB currently ranks as the most valuable bank brand in the Middle East and Africa, according to Brand Finance Magazine.
QNB Group has an active community support program and sponsors various social, educational and sporting events.
